chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah will punish the tongue with a punishment with which He does not punish any of the other body parts. So it will say, "O Lord! You have punished me with a punishment with which You did not punish anything else."'

So it will be said to him: 'A word came out from you and it reached the east and west of the earth, so unlawful blood was shed because of it, and unlawful wealth was seized, and the private parts were violated; and by My Honour and My Majesty! I will surely punish you with a punishment with which I do not punish anything else from your body parts.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the tongue punished more severely than other body parts in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to emphasize the 'weight' of speech in Shia ethics, where the tongue is treated as the primary agent of action due to its far-reaching influence. The Prophet’s explanation that a single utterance can trigger bloodshed, wealth seizure, or sexual violation underscores the concept of 'tadabbur' (reflection) on the causal chain of words. This highlights the scholarly view that preserving the tongue is not merely about silence, but about preventing the cascade of major sins (kabirah) initiated by speech.
